summary: The sample implements the screening flow end-to-end: seeding, storing embeddings on documents, creating a DocumentDB cosmosSearch vector index (via a PyMongo fallback), performing $search/cosmosSearch vector queries and $regex fuzzy matches, consolidating candidate sets, scoring, and returning a structured report via a FastAPI /screen endpoint. Unit tests pass locally and no secrets are committed. Findings: (1) the sample did not integrate LangChain even though the starter prompt asked for a 'LangChain agent' (builder omission), (2) the app issues unprefiltered regex queries with no text/search index (risk of collection scans), (3) no retry/backoff or batching logic for writes/remote calls, (4) index-creation and index-parameter tuning are present but README lacks guidance for scaling, and (5) infra-as-code for provisioning the DocumentDB cluster is missing. I list line-level evidence, the smallest fixes, a reconciliation of checklist vs discovered public guidance, decision reviews, and documentation gaps the product team should address.

requirement_results.requirement: Implement the screening agent in Python with LangChain as a single agent that takes a screening request and carries it through searching, consolidation, scoring and the report.
requirement_results.evidence: src/app.py implements a /screen FastAPI endpoint and scoring logic but contains no LangChain imports or usage (see app.py lines 1-16 and the endpoint implementation at lines 34-97). requirements.txt contains langchain, but code does not use it.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add minimal LangChain integration (e.g., instantiate a LangChain RetrievalQA or Agent that uses a DocumentDB retriever and call it from the /screen handler) or update code comments/README to explain why LangChain is omitted; prefer adding a small wrapper that uses LangChain's retriever API.

requirement_results.requirement: Store sanctions list entries as documents in Azure DocumentDB with each entry's embedding held on the document, and create a cosmosSearch vector index on the embedding field in code through a MongoDB driver with dimensions matching the embedding model used.
requirement_results.evidence: src/seed.py sets d['embedding'] for each document (seed.py lines 47-60) and upserts docs (replace_one at lines 61-63). scripts/create_vector_index.py sends a createIndexes command with cosmosSearchOptions and dimensions=1536 (create_vector_index.py lines 12-25). events show createIndexes succeeded and index exists (events: documentdb_list_indexes result).

requirement_results.requirement: On each screening request, embed the request with the same embedding model and run a vector similarity search in Azure DocumentDB with $search / cosmosSearch, returning the top candidate entries and their similarity scores.
requirement_results.evidence: app.py computes an embedding via openai.Embedding.create (app.py lines 41-46) and runs a $search aggregation with cosmosSearch and projects $meta 'searchScore' (app.py pipeline lines 48-52, aggregation call at line 53).

requirement_results.requirement: On each screening request, also run $regex-based fuzzy matching queries against the sanctions entries' text fields (e.g. name) in Azure DocumentDB and return the matching entries as candidates.
requirement_results.evidence: app.py compiles a regex and executes a find that matches name and alt_names ($regex and $elemMatch) (app.py lines 68-76).

requirement_results.requirement: Consolidate the vector search results and the $regex results into a single set of candidate matches for the request.
requirement_results.evidence: app.py builds a candidates dict from vector results then merges regex hits into the same dict before scoring (app.py lines 55-66 and 72-82).

requirement_results.requirement: Score each candidate match, producing a match confidence that draws on the vector similarity result and the $regex match evidence.
requirement_results.evidence: app.py uses combine_scores(...) to compute a combined score (app.py lines 86-94) and utils.combine_scores implements the weighting (src/utils.py lines 16-18).

requirement_results.requirement: Return a structured screening report (e.g. a typed object or JSON) listing each candidate match with its match confidence and a recommended action.
requirement_results.evidence: Pydantic models Candidate and ScreenResponse are defined (app.py lines 22-32) and the endpoint returns ScreenResponse with candidates (app.py return at lines 96-97).

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: .env.example lists DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY (app/.env.example lines 2-3) and code reads DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY from environment (src/db.py line 11, app.py lines 41-46, seed.py line 14). No secrets appear in source.

requirement_results.requirement: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example contains placeholders for DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY, EMBEDDING_MODEL, EMBEDDING_DIM and threshold/weight settings (app/.env.example lines 2-9).

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: Default embedding model is text-embedding-3-small (app.py and seed.py, EMBEDDING_MODEL default at line 11 in app.py and line 14 in seed.py) and the create_vector_index script sets dimensions: 1536 (scripts/create_vector_index.py line 20). .env.example also documents EMBEDDING_DIM=1536 (app/.env.example line 5).

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: scripts/create_vector_index.py sets vector-hnsw parameters (scripts/create_vector_index.py lines 18-24). README documents how to run the index-creation script (README.md lines 31-36) but does not explain parameter choices or provide guidance for tuning for larger datasets.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a short README section describing why the sample uses vector-hnsw with m=16/efConstruction=64 for small demos, point to the Vector Search docs, and show example parameter changes (or an alternative vector-ivf example) and when to move to DiskANN.

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: src/db.py implements a module-level singleton _client and get_client() that reuses MongoClient(uri) (src/db.py lines 5-16).

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: src/seed.py upserts documents idempotently using replace_one(upsert=True) (seed.py lines 61-63) and was executed in verification (events: 'Seeded 200 documents into sample_banking_18.sanctions'). The seed script does not create the vector index; index creation is handled by scripts/create_vector_index.py and by a separate MCP attempt in verification.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Make the seed script optionally create the vector index idempotently (call createIndexes with handling for 'index exists') or provide a single idempotent 'bootstrap' script that seeds and creates/verifies the index.

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: app.py checks for empty name and returns 400 (app.py lines 34-37). It checks OPENAI_API_KEY and raises HTTP 500 if absent (app.py lines 41-44). However, the code does not catch exceptions from the embedding API call (openai.Embedding.create at app.py line 45), so embedding-service failures will surface as an unhandled exception and 500 without a clear JSON detail.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Wrap the openai.Embedding.create call with try/except and raise an HTTPException with a clear error message explaining embedding failure and how to remediate (e.g., check OPENAI_API_KEY, network).

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: The $search pipeline projects $meta 'searchScore' (app.py pipeline lines 49-51), vec_results are used to populate vector_score (app.py lines 58-66), and the Candidate model includes match_confidence and reasons with vector_score (app.py lines 22-32 and 86-94).

requirement_results.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt.
requirement_results.evidence: requirements.txt pins some packages explicitly (fastapi==0.95.2, uvicorn==0.22.0, python-dotenv==1.0.0, pytest==7.4.0) but uses ranges for others (pymongo>=4.3,<5.0 and openai>=1.0.0,<3.0) (requirements.txt lines 1-7).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Pin exact tested versions in requirements.txt (or add a constraints.txt) and record the versions used during verification in README/test artifacts.

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: tests/test_utils.py is a pure-unit test for cosine/combination logic (tests/test_utils.py lines 4-16). The CI/verification run executed pytest and showed '2 passed' (events.jsonl run at entry where pytest succeeded).

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: There is no infra/ or Bicep/Terraform artifact in the repository, and README lists infra/ as optional but no templates are shipped (README.md lines 20-23).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a minimal infra artifact (Bicep or Terraform) that targets Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with parameters for tier/region/storage; the 'documentdb-azure-deployment' skill provides Bicep examples — include a small example in infra/ and point to it from README.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: README includes what it shows, prerequisites and quickstart run instructions (README.md lines 5-15 and 24-35) but does not give explicit cleanup/uninstall steps (no commands to drop sample collections or remove seeded data).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a 'clean-up' section to README with commands to drop the sample collection and any recommended steps to remove seeded data and indexes (or an optional 'destroy' script).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: README title and content refer to 'Azure DocumentDB' (README.md line 1 and lines 3-9). .env.example uses the cluster hostname pattern mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com consistent with the managed product (app/.env.example line 2).

checks.practice: One MongoClient per process, reuse across requests
checks.evidence: src/db.py implements a module-level singleton _client and get_client() that returns the same MongoClient instance (src/db.py lines 5-16).
checks.source: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python

sources.title: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python

checks.practice: Enforce TLS and recommended connection options (tls=true, auth mechanism and sensible timeouts/pool sizing)
checks.evidence: src/db.py calls MongoClient(uri) without explicit connection options or documented maxPoolSize/timeouts; no code sets connection options (src/db.py line 15). .env.example documents only URI but no connection-option environment variables (app/.env.example lines 2-9).
checks.fix: Pass recommended options from environment into MongoClient (e.g., maxPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, tls=true if not in URI) and document required flags in .env.example.

checks.practice: Use a driver version the service supports and document/test it
checks.evidence: requirements.txt uses a range for pymongo (pymongo>=4.3,<5.0) rather than pinning the tested version (requirements.txt lines 1-7). Learn docs include 'Tested driver version' notes (e.g., Quickstart pages list tested PyMongo 4.19.0).
checks.source: Quickstart: Connect Django MongoDB backend to Azure DocumentDB (tested driver notes)
checks.fix: Pin the specific PyMongo version tested during verification or add a constraints.txt that records the exact versions used; mention the tested version in README.

sources.title: Quickstart: Connect Django MongoDB backend to Azure DocumentDB

checks.evidence: scripts/create_vector_index.py issues createIndexes with cosmosSearchOptions kind 'vector-hnsw' and parameters (scripts/create_vector_index.py lines 12-25). events show the index was created and listed (events: documentdb_list_indexes result).

checks.evidence: app.py builds a $search pipeline with cosmosSearch and projects {$meta: 'searchScore'} (app.py lines 48-52, pipeline execution at line 53).
checks.source: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Ensure vectors are stored as number[] and one vector index per path
checks.evidence: Seed documents store embedding as a list (seed.py lines 47-60), create_vector_index uses key embedding path and only one vector index was created (documentdb_list_indexes shows one embedding_vector_idx).
checks.source: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Avoid unbounded full-collection regex scans; prefer text/search indexes or prefilters
checks.evidence: app.py executes an unprefiltered regex find on name and alt_names (app.py lines 68-72). The index list contains only _id_ and embedding_vector_idx (events documentdb_list_indexes), so the regex find will cause a collection scan for name matches.
checks.fix: Create a text/search index or a normalized name field with a standard index or use createSearchIndexes with analyzers; at minimum add a prefilter (e.g., country) and/or an indexed normalized_name field to scope regex queries.

checks.practice: Return which index/search matched and include searchScore and stored document
checks.evidence: The pipeline includes returnStoredSource and the app projects $meta searchScore; candidates include vector_score and regex_score in 'reasons' (app.py lines 49-52 and 86-94).
checks.source: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

sources.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: When using LangChain, prefer pre_filter (or driver-level filter) to narrow candidates inside vector search
checks.evidence: The sample does not use LangChain so pre_filter integration is not present; app.py does not supply a prefilter to the vector $search (app.py pipeline lines 48-52).
checks.source: Use LangChain on Azure with Azure DocumentDB
checks.fix: If you integrate LangChain, use its pre_filter option to push filters into the cosmosSearch query (e.g., filter by country or a partition key) rather than post-filtering after kNN.

sources.title: Use LangChain on Azure with Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Use projections to return only fields needed for the response
checks.evidence: The regex find call uses projection={'name': 1} (app.py line 71) and the $search pipeline projects score and document (app.py lines 51-52).

checks.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff and ensure writes are idempotent
checks.evidence: There is no retry/backoff wrapper around network calls or DB writes; seed.py uses replace_one which is idempotent for seed writes but the app has no generic retry policy for transient query/aggregation failures (seed.py lines 61-63; no retry code elsewhere).
checks.fix: Implement a retry wrapper for transient faults (exponential backoff + jitter) for network/DB operations and centralize configuration via environment variables; ensure writes that are retried are idempotent.

decision_reviews.comment: Approval to proceed with 'ready_with_gaps' is consistent with the run: the app built and verification steps completed with some documentation and robustness gaps.
Choosing Python 3.11 is consistent with the prompt and environment. Files and tests were written for Python and executed successfully in the run.
Choice of PyMongo and singleton client was implemented (src/db.py) and the documentdb-driver skill was loaded (events shows load_skill).

Embedding model and dimension were chosen by model_default (text-embedding-3-small / 1536) and the code/indices use 1536 dims. There is no single authoritative DocumentDB doc that mandates a particular embedding model; this is an application choice. Because the reason source is 'model_default' and no authoritative public doc prescribes the model, the decision is inherently unverifiable from DocumentDB docs alone.
Reading DOCUMENTDB_URI from the environment was implemented in src/db.py (line 11) and matches the skill_md guidance; events show the decision was logged and code uses the env var.
Providing FastAPI + CLI is implemented (src/app.py and scripts/demo_screen.py). The decision is consistent and evidence is present.

The builder attempted to create the index via the MCP helper as recorded; events show documentdb_create_index was called and failed (ToolExecutionException: management tools disabled). The attempt is visible in events and the decision to try MCP is supported by the tool result.

Choosing vector weight 0.7 / regex 0.3 is reasonable for a sample but based on model_default. There's no DocumentDB doc prescribing those weights; the choice is defensible but subjective and should be documented with a note that thresholds require tuning against labeled data.

Relaxing the openai requirement in requirements.txt is justified by the pip install error; events show the pip install initially failed for openai==1.8.5 and that requirements were updated and install succeeded.
Running the seed script was executed and recorded (events show 'Seeded 200 documents'). The seed is idempotent (replace_one upsert).
The MCP helper failed and the builder used the PyMongo createIndexes fallback (scripts/create_vector_index.py). Events record the exceptions and the successful db.command createIndexes execution.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No public DocumentDB guidance tells a sample which embedding model/provider to pick or which embedding dimension to use; the sample must assume a model (the builder chose OpenAI text-embedding-3-small / 1536).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Searches for 'embedding model dimensions DocumentDB' and the vector-search docs; installed skills were consulted (documentdb-vector-search).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The build committed to 1536 dims and created an index with dimensions=1536. If a user picks a different embedding model, index creation or queries may fail or return errors (dimension mismatch).
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Agent-kit rule: 'Samples MUST set EMBEDDING_MODEL and EMBEDDING_DIM in .env.example and use EMBEDDING_DIM when creating vector indexes; if the embedding provider is unspecified, default to text-embedding-3-small with 1536 dims and document that this default is only for the sample.'

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No explicit public DocumentDB guidance on idempotent createIndexes handling (error semantics when index exists) surfaced in quick discovery; builder created a create-vector-index script but seed.py does not create or verify the index.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Searches for 'createIndexes idempotent Azure DocumentDB' and review of createIndexes examples in vector-search docs.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder attempted the MCP automation, it failed, and they used a PyMongo createIndexes fallback. The repo now contains two separate steps (seed, create_index) which a user must run in order. This increases friction and risk of out-of-sync index parameters.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A sample 'bootstrap' script that idempotently (a) creates the collection (if missing), (b) calls createIndexes with cosmosSearchOptions and handles 'index already exists' responses, and (c) waits/verifies index readiness via listIndexes or a helper; include a short code snippet showing the createIndexes payload and the check for existing index.

doc_gaps.topic: Regex vs full-text recommendations for fuzzy matching
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The public docs do show createSearchIndexes and analyzers, but the sample relied on unprefiltered regex searches without a documented mitigation in README. Guidance that an agent could use to prefer createSearchIndexes (edgeGram/ASCII-folding analyzers) over raw regex for large datasets should be surfaced.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Full-text search docs and vector-search docs (learn.microsoft.com 'full-text search custom analyzers' and 'vector-search').
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The app issues unbounded regex finds that could cause COLLSCAN on larger datasets; the sample's README does not warn users to create a text/search index or to prefilter, increasing the risk that a user will run costly queries in production.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short README section: 'Avoid full-collection regex in production' with (1) an example of creating a createSearchIndexes text index with an edgeGram analyzer for name prefix matching, (2) show how to materialize a normalized_name field and index it, and (3) show the preferred pattern of prefiltering by country or partition key before running cosmosSearch.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The sample lacks a centrally configured retry/backoff policy for DB or embedding calls; DocumentDB best-practices note retries and idempotency but a ready-to-use sample policy was not included.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Reliability in Azure DocumentDB docs and retries best-practices pages.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Transient network or service errors (embedding API, DB aggregation) are not handled uniformly; this increases flakiness and exposes users to unhelpful 500s.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Provide an 'http_db_retry' helper in the agent kit demonstrating exponential backoff + jitter for DB/HTTP calls (configurable via env: RETRY_MAX, RETRY_BASE_MS), and example usage in seed.py and app.py around network calls.

doc_gaps.topic: README guidance for index parameter tuning & scaling
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Although the vector index parameters are in code, README lacks a short explanation of what to change as data size grows (numLists, nProbes for IVF; m/efConstruction for HNSW; DiskANN when dataset becomes large) and how to change cluster tier.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Users may run the sample, then try to scale without understanding which parameters to change or when to increase cluster tier; they might pick incorrect parameters and run into memory limits or poor recall/latency.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a 'Tuning vector index parameters' README subsection that (a) explains m/efConstruction/efSearch/nlist/nProbes tradeoffs, (b) gives numeric examples for 200, 10k, 100k+ docs, and (c) shows how to change createIndexes JSON and when to prefer DiskANN and to scale the cluster tier (M30+).

doc_gaps.topic: Infrastructure examples for mongoClusters resource type
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The sample lacks an infra-as-code example targeting Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters. Readiness findings flagged confusion between databaseAccounts (Cosmos RU model) and mongoClusters (vCore-managed DocumentDB).
doc_gaps.where_searched: ARM/Bicep templates and CLI docs (learn.microsoft.com searches found mongoClusters templates).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Without infra examples, builders may attempt to provision the wrong resource type (databaseAccounts) and create an incompatible cluster; this is a high-risk point for publishable samples.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add an infra/ folder with a minimal Bicep file that deploys Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with parameters for tier/region, plus a README paragraph: 'This sample targets the vCore DocumentDB mongoClusters resource; do not use databaseAccounts.'

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No DocumentDB-specific guidance was found to confirm or deny the pattern of storing embedding_model/embedding_version with each document and enforcing compatibility at query time.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Searches for 'DocumentDB embedding_version per document' and similar queries returned no decisive guidance.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample does not store embedding version metadata. If users later change embedding model, older vectors and the index may become incompatible, causing subtle failures or poor matches.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short doc page recommending storing embedding metadata (model name, version, timestamp) alongside embeddings, recommending a reindex/recompute workflow, and showing sample fields and a query-time guard.

doc_gaps.topic: Agent-kit guidance: prefer createSearchIndexes and analyzers over raw regex
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Although DocumentDB docs show custom analyzers, the agent-kit lacks a succinct recipe for building name-matching analyzers (lowerCase + asciiFolding + edgeGram) for sanctions lists.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Full-text custom analyzers docs and the vector-search skill resources.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builder used simple regex matching in the sample; a compact example in the agent-kit would have guided them to a more efficient approach and avoided full-collection scans.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short sample showing createSearchIndexes JSON that defines a 'name-search' index using lowerCase + asciiFolding + edgeGram filters and an example $search query that uses the index for fuzzy/prefix matching.
